meta.filePurpose: Functional design spec for a Morningstar MC6 Pro pedalboard controller layout
notes: This file is a human-readable design plan, not a direct MC6 Pro import file.
It is intended to capture desired functionality before converting it into Morningstar Editor presets and MIDI messages.
The current working backups show active banks including Home, Ableton, Pedals, Reverb, Tremolo, Delay, and Doubler.

designGoals: Use the MC6 Pro as the main controller for pedal toggles, looper transport, and bank navigation.
Keep the home bank simple and performance-safe.
Use consistent switch behavior across banks wherever possible.
Reserve room for long press, release, and toggle behaviors once pedal MIDI details are confirmed.

alwaysOnList.summary: Track sounds that should normally remain engaged so the controller logic can preserve that expectation.

implementationNotes: Morningstar presets can send multiple MIDI messages from a single switch action.
Toggle presets should define both ON and OFF states explicitly.
Navigation actions should be separated from sound-critical actions where possible.

midiChannelPlan.guidingRule: Reserve MIDI channels 1 through 5 for Ableton and software-facing control, then start hardware pedals at channel 6.

notes: Both reverb and tremolo sides live on this one pedal channel.
Standard MIDI 1.0 provides 16 channels per MIDI port or connection, numbered 1 through 16.
Audio recording itself does not use MIDI channels, but reserving channels for Ableton or other software targets is a clean routing choice.
Strymon pedals often default to MIDI channel 1, so each pedal should be reconfigured to match this plan.
Using one channel per physical pedal keeps MC6 programming easier to reason about and troubleshoot.
Logical controls for Flint reverb and Flint tremolo should share the same channel because they are two sides of one pedal.

Based on current official Strymon support documentation, Flint v2, EC-1, and Deco can all be assigned across MIDI channels 1 through 16. Channels 4 through 16 are typically set by putting the pedal in MIDI channel mode and sending a Program Change on the desired channel.
The re-exported Morningstar backup after manual editor changes should be treated as the controller-settings baseline.
In the backup JSON, Omniports 1 through 3 use internal type value 5 and Omniport 4 uses internal type value 1.
Relay Port A is currently used as the analog tempo output for the Unicorn-style univibe tap input.

universalPageButtons.summary: Every visible page should reserve the third switch for Tap Tempo and the sixth switch for Back/Home.
universalPageButtons.purpose: This avoids getting lost in bank and page navigation and gives the same two escape hatches everywhere in the controller.

slotRule.sixthSwitchOnEveryPage: Back on release, Home on long hold

implementationNotes: The top-right switch should go to the parent context page on release and jump to global Home on long hold.
Tap Tempo should stay on the bottom-right switch of every visible page, which maps to C, I, O, and U in the editor lettering scheme.
The four remaining positions on each page become the variable slots for pedal or song functions.
In the generated JSON workflow, the Back/Home buttons should be treated as templated through one shared generator helper rather than edited individually in every bank.
Tap buttons should use the plain label Tap.
Back buttons should use the literal label \- Back.
The current generated Tap macro should send MC6 MIDI Clock Tap, Relay Port A Sync Clock 8 Taps, and Flint remote tap.

pageColorTiers.summary: Bank background colors should reflect navigation depth so the user can visually tell what level of the controller they are on.
implementationNotes: Use bank color 2 for Home, 49 for Ableton, 8 for Pedals, 127 for Songs, 39 for Reverb, 58 for Tremolo, 61 for Delay, and 4 for Doubler.

toggleStateBehavior.summary: Scene-style sound buttons should use controller-side toggle state so the active selection can be shown on the MC6 display.
implementationNotes: Use Toggle Reset Groups on the Reverb, Tremolo, and Delay banks so only one sound level stays visually active at a time without letting Tap or Back clear the strip state.
The current Tremolo bank should use slot A as a Message Scroll preset for Flint tap subdivisions instead of a Light preset.
That subdivision idea may not be useful with the current controller-side Remote Tap workflow. If a scroll control is needed before moving to MIDI clock, Trem Type is a better immediate candidate.
Enable remembered preset toggle states in controller settings so the active scene can remain visible when navigating away and back.
Pos: Both only duplicates the same message in both toggle positions. It does not create a real on/off toggle by itself.
For true toggle behavior, split the logic between Position 1 and Position 2.
Position 1 should be the explicit on or selected scene macro.
Position 2 should explicitly undo, bypass, or reset what Position 1 turned on.
Use button backgrounds 5, 44, 46, and 3 for Light, Medium, Medium Heavy, and Heavy respectively, with white text.
Use Tap styling of tan background 34, black text 0, and lime strip 1.
Use LED color 9 for off state and LED toggle color 1 for on state, based on the manually adjusted Reverb Light sample in the latest backup.
For the current Strymon setup, Reverb Position 2 should bypass reverb, Tremolo Position 2 should bypass tremolo, and Delay Position 2 should bypass the pedal.
Do not use bank-level Clear Preset Toggles on these effect banks, because pressing Tap or Back can clear the remembered strip state while the pedal remains on.
Bank Jump on Long Press executes when the switch is released, so it can feel like Long Press Release in practice.

navigationPolicy: Bank 0 should be the performance-safe landing page.
Top-level home actions should jump into deeper banks instead of packing too much into one page.
Long-press actions should be used for setup or less-common functions.

currentPlannedBankOrganization.summary: Current working organization uses a contextual hierarchy: global and contextual home pages in low-numbered banks, deeper pedal pages higher up.

displayBankMap.name: Delay More
displayBankMap.role: Additional EC-1 manual editing and preset scroll controls

navigationModel: Home -> Ableton -> Ableton Guitar or Ableton Voice
Home -> Pedals -> Reverb or Tremolo or Delay or Doubler
Home -> Pedals -> Delay long hold -> Delay Manual -> Delay More
futureReservedSpace: Leave room in low banks for additional contextual home pages.
Leave room in high banks for future pedal pages and reusable macro banks.

strymonFirstPassArchitecture.scope: Current first pass is focused on Strymon pedals, with Flint designed first.

currentScope.summary: Version 1 should focus on the four core settings per effect family rather than a larger custom preset catalog.
futureExpansion: Add custom preset slots after the four core settings are stable.
Use a second page or additional pages for Custom 1 through Custom 4 style presets when needed.
Keep the first page focused on the four go-to sounds for quick live access.

recommendedArchitecture: Use Program Change for whole-pedal Flint scenes such as Home reset, All Defaults, and song shortcuts.
Use direct MIDI CC macros for live Reverb and Tremolo banks so each side can be controlled independently.
Avoid double tap behaviors in the first build. Use Press and Long Press only.
Keep the top-level layout at 6 presets per bank whenever possible.

notes: Use the same level naming wherever possible so song buttons and pedal banks feel consistent.
The current generated Doubler bank uses the same four-level layout as Delay for speed of live use.

recommendedHomeBehavior.summary: Going Home should recall default scene presets on all Strymon pedals.
recommendedHomeBehavior.defaultResetConcept: Each pedal should have a saved default preset that represents the shared baseline sound. For Flint, the recommended baseline is Reverb Medium plus Trem Light.

flint.importantConstraint: Flint Program Change recalls the current state of the pedal, so a saved Flint preset always represents both reverb and tremolo together.

recommendedDefaultPreset.description: Default Flint scene used when returning Home.

savedOptions.midiClockDivision: x1/4 unless a song needs another division
savedOptions.expressionAssignment: Choose one default assignment or leave neutral for the first pass

notes: This export confirms that a real Flint preset can be inspected from a Strymon sysex export.
The exported values are useful as a reference, but they are not a direct 1:1 copy of the MIDI CC values sent by the MC6.

liveControlStrategy.summary: For live pedal banks, each button should send a full side-specific macro so the result is explicit and repeatable.

notes: These are recommended starting values and should be tuned by ear once the Flint is connected.
Every reverb button keeps the reverb voice locked to 70s Plate and leaves tremolo untouched.

settings.name: Light
settings.intent: Low-ambience plate that stays out of the way.

settings.name: Medium
settings.intent: Primary always-on reverb level and Home default target.

settings.name: Medium Heavy
settings.intent: Bigger plate without turning into a wash.

settings.name: Heavy
settings.intent: Large plate texture for featured sections.

notes: These are recommended starting values and should be tuned by ear once the Flint is connected.
The level macros below intentionally do not change trem speed or clock division.
Because the MC6 Pro is expected to send MIDI clock, rhythmic division should usually be managed by the default Flint preset or song scenes, not by the Light/Medium/Heavy buttons.

settings.name: Light
settings.intent: Always-on photo trem with subtle motion.

settings.name: Medium
settings.intent: Noticeable but still general-purpose photo trem.

settings.name: Medium Heavy
settings.intent: Stronger pulse that still keeps the guitar grounded.

settings.name: Heavy
settings.intent: Pronounced photo trem for featured sections.

expressionStrategy.summary: The current generated MC6 file uses controller-side expression on Omniport 4, with one bank-specific expression preset per Flint page.
recommendedApproach: Use the Reverb bank expression preset to send Flint CC18 Mix and CC20 Decay together.
Use the Tremolo bank expression preset to send Flint CC12 Intensity and a small amount of CC15 Boost.
Keep pedal-side Flint expression assignments as a later option only if a future revision needs deeper internal preset morphing.
currentGeneratedAssignments: Reverb bank: Mix 30 to 96 plus Decay 52 to 120
Tremolo bank: Intensity 32 to 127 plus Boost 64 to 78

ec1.recommendedControlModel: Use saved EC-1 presets via Program Change for most sound selection. Reserve CC messages for tap tempo, expression, utility functions, or rare live tweaks.

presetNumberingPlan.summary: Reserve EC-1 preset locations 1 through 16 for the main Morningstar workflow.
implementationNotes: These are Program Change-driven recalls on the EC-1.
Avoid Program Change 0 for this lane because EC-1 reserves it for the Favorite setting.
Avoid Program Change 127 because EC-1 uses it for Manual Mode.
Some controllers and apps display Program Change numbering starting at 1 instead of 0, so the Morningstar Editor values should always be verified against the actual recalled EC-1 preset.

notes: Current Strymon Nixie 2 support documentation lists Flint v2 and Deco v2, but does not list EC-1.
Design the EC-1 library around pedal-stored presets and MIDI recall rather than a Nixie-based editing workflow for now.

recommendedDefaultPreset.description: Default EC-1 scene used when returning Home.

notes: EC-1 is much simpler than Flint or Deco because it is one effect, so preset recall is usually enough.
If you keep your main EC-1 sounds in MIDI preset locations 0-127, one Program Change is enough to recall them.
Delay Light is the current always-on slapback sound and should send CC63 = 0 on Position 1 so MIDI Clock follow is off.
Delay Light should send CC63 = 127 on Position 2 so clock follow is restored when that toggle is turned off.
Delay Medium, Delay Medium Heavy, and Delay Heavy should each send CC63 = 127 on Position 1 so choosing another delay sound restores clock follow.
The current generated Tap buttons should not send direct CC93 tap to the EC-1 anymore.
Tap should update the MC6 internal MIDI clock and relay sync instead, so Delay Light can stay fixed while the other delay presets continue to follow tempo.
The current generated Delay bank expression preset on Omniport 4 should send EC-1 CC16 Mix and CC14 Repeats.
The current generated Delay expression ranges are intended to feel most dramatic on the Heavy delay sound, moving from a strong lead repeat into a wetter and more blooming texture.

proposedDelayManualBank.summary: A future Delay Manual bank can turn the MC6 into a button-and-scroll front panel for the EC-1 while leaving the regular Delay bank optimized for preset recall.

recommendedScrollBehaviors.mix: Short musical sweep from dry-ish to fairly wet
recommendedScrollBehaviors.repeats: Short musical sweep from one slap to more sustaining repeats
recommendedScrollBehaviors.tapeAge: Cleaner to darker or older tape texture
recommendedScrollBehaviors.mechanics: Stable to more warble or machine texture
recommendedScrollBehaviors.presetScroll: Bounded PC scroll through a curated preset range, ideally 1 through 16

expressionNote: Because the current MC6 expression setup is bank-wide, one manual page should only have one expression job at a time.

If expression is added to a manual workflow later, the clean pattern is separate sub-pages like Delay Mix, Delay Repeats, Delay Age, and Delay Mechanics, each with its own Omniport 4 expression assignment.
importantConstraints: Dry Mode and Spillover are global EC-1 settings, not normal live MIDI-scrolled parameters.
The first practical version of Delay Manual should stay mostly button-and-scroll based.
implementedNow: Long Press on the Delay button in Pedals jumps to Delay Manual.
Delay Manual currently provides Mix, Repeats, Tape Age, and Mechanics message scroll presets.
Long Press on Mech in Delay Manual jumps to Delay More.
Delay More currently provides Rec Level, Preamp voice, Tap Division, and Preset scroll.

deco.importantConstraint: Deco Program Change recalls the current state of the pedal, so a saved Deco preset always represents both the Tape Saturation side and the Doubletracker side together.

recommendedDefaultPreset.description: Default Deco scene used when returning Home.

savedOptions.mode: Classic unless Cassette is intentionally needed
savedOptions.wideStereo: Off for mono rigs unless a song needs stereo spread
savedOptions.expressionAssignment: Choose one neutral default assignment or leave expression-specific presets for later

currentGeneratedDoublerBank.summary: The current generated MC6 file treats Doubler like Delay for a fast first pass.
behaviorNotes: Position 1 recalls the chosen Deco preset, forces the overall Deco path on with CC33 value 127, and then turns the Doubletracker side on with CC16 value 127.
Position 2 turns the Doubletracker side off with CC16 value 0.
Long Press sends CC97 = 127 for Auto-Flange.
Long Press Release sends CC97 = 0 so the flange drops out when the hold ends.

liveControlStrategy.summary: For live pedal banks, each button should send a side-specific Deco macro so Tape Saturation and Doubletracker can be changed independently.

notes: These are recommended starting values and should be tuned by ear once the pedal is connected.
Every tape button leaves the Doubletracker side untouched.

settings.name: Medium
settings.intent: More obvious tape richness while staying general-purpose.

settings.name: Heavy
settings.intent: Featured tape drive for bigger sections.

notes: These are recommended starting values and should be tuned by ear once the pedal is connected.
Every Doubletracker button leaves the Tape Saturation side untouched.
The third sound slot is intentionally called Special rather than Heavy so it can represent a featured doubler texture rather than just more of the same.
The Flange button can be a dedicated CC97 command or can live on long press if you want to keep the top-level layout simpler.

settings.name: Special
settings.intent: Featured doubler texture such as a bigger widening sound, slap-style repeat, or standout solo treatment.

settings.name: Flange
behaviorNotes: Best on long press or press-and-hold.
Release behavior can send CC97 value 0 if a clean exit is needed.

expressionStrategy.summary: The current generated MC6 file uses controller-side expression on Omniport 4 for the Doubler page.
recommendedApproach: Use the Doubler bank expression preset to send Doubletracker Lag Time, Blend, and Wobble together.
Keep pedal-side Deco expression assignments as a future option only if a later revision needs more complex morphing.
currentGeneratedAssignments: Doubler bank: Lag Time 18 to 110 plus Blend 30 to 108 plus Wobble 0 to 72

reusablePresetLibraryArchitecture.summary: Use higher-numbered MC6 banks as reusable action libraries for each Strymon pedal, then trigger those presets from visible banks such as Main Pedals and Songs.
whyThisWorks: It centralizes the pedal logic so the same actions can be reused by pedal banks, global utility banks, and song banks.
It reduces copy-and-paste when a sound definition changes.
It supports explicit control, which matches the goal of avoiding accidental or conflicting taps.

notes: Visible Home buttons on C, I, O, and U should call the Global Home macro.
Visible Tap Tempo buttons on F, L, R, and X should call the Global Tap Tempo macro.

contents: Preset 4: Reverb Medium Heavy CC macro
Preset 6: Reverb Off or Reverb Expression Selector
Preset 3: Trem Medium Heavy CC macro
Preset 5: Trem Off or Trem Expression Selector
Examples: Reverb Mix, Reverb Decay, Reverb Pre-Delay, Trem Intensity, Dual Morph
Preset 5: EC-1 future custom preset recall
Preset 6: EC-1 Tap, Infinite, or Expression utility

callingModel.mainPedalsBank: Visible control banks can bank-jump into the pedal-specific library banks or call selected library presets directly.
callingModel.songBanks: Song presets can execute multiple library presets in sequence so one song button can build a full cross-pedal scene.
callingModel.homeBank: Home can call the default preset for each pedal library to restore the rig to a known baseline.

songProgrammingRule.summary: Song presets should be deterministic and explicit.
recommendedOrder: First call any pedal-wide default PC scenes needed to establish a known base state.
Then call side-specific CC macros that customize only the parts that should change for the song.
Then send tempo and any global utility commands.
songProgrammingRule.importantWarning: If a song preset does not send a message for a pedal or pedal side, that part will usually remain in its previous state. If a song should guarantee a default sound, it must explicitly call the default for that pedal or side.

exampleFlow: Call Flint Reverb Medium Heavy CC macro
Call Flint Trem Medium CC macro
Call EC-1 preset via Program Change
Call Deco default preset or Tape Default action to establish the base Deco state
Call Deco Doubler CC macro for the desired solo or song texture
Send preset song tempo from MC6
notes: If Deco tape saturation should remain at default, the song should still explicitly establish that default rather than relying on whatever happened previously.
For Flint, the song can either use CC macros for both sides or call one full Flint preset if the exact combined scene is already saved on the pedal.

futureCustomPresetExpansion.summary: After the four core sounds are stable, each pedal bank can add Custom preset slots without changing the overall architecture.
examples: Page 1: Light, Medium, Home, Medium Heavy, Heavy, Tap Tempo
Page 2: Custom 1, Custom 2, Home, Custom 3, Custom 4, Tap Tempo
notes: Flint v2 and Deco v2 custom presets can be auditioned, edited, saved, exported, and organized in Nixie 2.
EC-1 custom presets should be treated as pedal-stored presets until Strymon adds Nixie 2 support.

designNotes: Reverb and Tremolo are intentionally separate entries even though they both target the Flint on MIDI channel 2.
This preserves independent live access to each Flint side.
Because Home and Tap Tempo are global on every page, only four content slots remain per page.
This makes a two-page Main Pedals bank the cleanest solution.

switches.label: Reverb
switches.desiredBehavior: Jump to the Flint Reverb control bank or page so reverb can be adjusted independently from tremolo.
implementationNotes: This entry targets Flint channel 2 but only calls reverb-side CC macros or reverb expression presets.

switches.label: Tremolo
switches.desiredBehavior: Jump to the Flint Tremolo control bank or page so tremolo can be adjusted independently from reverb.
implementationNotes: This entry also targets Flint channel 2 but only calls tremolo-side CC macros or tremolo expression presets.

switches.label: Home

questionsToResolve: What are the exact pedal brands and models you want the MC6 Pro to control?
Which pedals are connected by 5-pin MIDI, TRS MIDI, USB MIDI, or via a MIDI box?
What MIDI channel should each pedal listen on?
Should each switch act as a toggle, a momentary command, a preset recall, or a multi-action macro?
Which actions should live on press versus long press versus release?
Do you want dedicated tap tempo, tuner, mute, bank up/down, and page left/right switches?
Should the MC6 Pro reflect pedal state with LED colors and toggle names?

workflow: Confirm the pedal inventory and MIDI channels.
Confirm desired switch behavior for each bank.
Translate this spec into Morningstar Editor-ready presets.
Optionally generate or modify the real MC6 Pro backup JSON.
